title.narrative: Provision of Life-saving and Life-sustaining Humanitarian Integrated Assistance for the Most Vulnerable Groups in Northwest Syria

description.narrative:
As part of TِAS emergency response and sustainable solutions, TAS will provide an integrated WASH, Edu, and SNFI intervention to support the most vulnerable due to the limited access to main services and to provide the emergency response as part of Cholera response in NWS. The project was designed to cover the gaps in WASH- Edu-SNFI for 19,531 beneficiaries living in 9 locations in Idleb. TAS intervention will fully coordinate with OCHA, clusters, and local actors in the targeted area. The planned intervention will mainstream protection especially (Do no harm) throughout the project cycle by considering the different needs of men, women, children, adolescents, adults, middle-aged adults, elders, and PwDs. TAS-integrated interventions will be as follow:
WASH: TAS designed this project as a sustainable approach and as a cholera response plan to support a total of 14,136 individuals, in 9 sites (8 IDP sites and 1 community) in Idleb with basic water, sanitation, and Hygiene activities including the establishment of more sustainable water supply mechanisms (elevated water tanks, water networks, and solar system), solid waste activities, and promoting hygiene and reducing water-related diseases (AWD/cholera). TAS will provide safe drinking water with necessary water quality tests (chlorination), provision of soap for hand washing, and Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), conducting The project locations are 9 locations as follows: - 3 camps in Kelly, Maaret Tamsrin(Cholera scale 4.67) - 2 camps in Bab El Hawa, Dana(Cholera scale 5.01) - 2 camps in Shekh Bahr, Maaret Tamsrin(Cholera scale 4.67) - one camp and one community in Kafr tanor, Maaret Tamsrin,(Cholera scale 4.67).
Edu: TAS aims to secure a safe environment for 5178 IDP children (5-17, 2837 B, 2341 G) in 6 camps schools in Dana and Ma'arrat Misrin which were established last year due to lack of educational services, and their fund ended, with no support during the upcoming semester. The camps’ schools are in Dana and Ma'arrat Misrin which will be supported by an integrated approach that focuses on providing life-saving education and protection assistance to crises-affected children to protect and promote the healthy environment in which they are located through providing integrated services in the education protection and WASH sectors. TAS will provide heating fuel for a total of 50 schools(10,734 children 5,841 B, 4,893 G), 6 of the project target and 44 other schools only for fuel as the other activities are supported by other organizations in (Ariha, Armanaz, Dana, Ehsem, Harim, Idleb, Jisr-Ash-Shugur, Kafr Takharim, Ma'arrat Misrin, Qourqeena, and Salqin). In addition, we will implement light maintenance for schools, especially the WASH facilities, so they will protect students from cholera also by providing and doubling the number of cleaning materials in the running cost that we supply to schools. To raise the quality of education, we will work to buy bags for students at the beginning of the second semester. In addition to paying teachers' stipends In order to increase access to CwDs in the targeted areas, the project will provide schools with tools for CwDs.
SNFI: TAS through CASH for winter will address the winterization requirements of the most vulnerable individuals and adapt to shocks anticipated in the winter season of 2022 / 2023, this winterization approach will boost the thermal comfort of homes (HHs) during the winter months. TAS will target 2 camps (which have a gap in providing winterization support): Al farhan(Doyouf Almaara) : 117 HHs. Al Hayat Al Jadida : 304 HHs. Each HH will receive $150 as a one-off CASH for winter distribution TAS will manage the distribution according to the voucher mechanism that guarantees fairness, while preserving the environment, taking into account the issues of security, safety, preservation, protection, and observing gender balance.
